answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with the stake slashed when two identities are proven to share one operator. A steady pulse of signed heartbeat proofs ties every voyage of transactions to a single staked key, so spawning thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of stakes. The summit of this cost curve is reached quickly: faking influence costs more than the influence is worth, while honest agents get their stake back.
